findings.summary: records.rs ends only 84 lines under the 1500 busy-file limit; the split is likely to be re-triggered soon
findings.evidence: 1416 production lines (test module at 1417-3644). The file went from 2543 production lines when the request was written to 3215 at base, about 670 lines in roughly a week, and has 7 landings a week. The core job/invocation/verification/outcome types (roughly lines 428-1027, about 600 lines) and the shared parts stay in records.rs. Moving them into their own submodule, as the reading's survey suggested, would leave real headroom instead of a margin of about 5%.

findings.summary: Submodule named `core` hides Rust's built-in `core` crate inside records and its submodules; it also holds host-error and decision-state types, not the core job types
findings.evidence: `mod core;` together with `use super::*;` in each submodule means an unqualified `core::…` path there resolves to records::core. Derive macros use `::core` and the tree compiles, but a name such as `decisions` or `host` would avoid the confusion. The file's own doc comment reads 'Host-error, decision-state and default-expectation records.'

summary: Pass. The change splits crates/athena-data/src/records.rs into five private submodules (core, introspection, work, throughput, plan), each re-exported with `pub use self::<mod>::*`. All results are from the snapshot. Measured the way code_health::measure_source does (total lines minus #[cfg(test)] modules), records.rs now has 1416 production lines: the file is 3644 lines and its test module runs from 1417 to the end. Before the split it had 3215. It is now under both the 2000 and the 1500/5-landings limits. The new files are 265, 549, 302, 374 and 336 lines, none with test modules. Running `git diff --minimal --numstat` of the base records.rs against each new file shows only 2 lines per file not taken from the base: a module doc comment and `use super::*;`. The only lines added to records.rs are the 11 module/re-export lines. So the move is order-preserving with no edits to code, serde attributes or schema constants. `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked` and `cargo test -p athena-data` pass, and Athena's recorded CI run shows fmt, clippy and the full test suite passing. AnyRecord, RecordError and check_record_file stay in records.rs unchanged. The CHANGELOG entry is under [Unreleased]. Two weak points: records.rs is only 84 lines under the 1500 busy limit, on a file that gained about 670 lines in roughly a week. And the new module is named `core`, the same as Rust's built-in `core` crate.
